a.text: Eight years ago...
Summer, 1086

steps.text: Residential district, the nomadic city of Kazdel, Kazdel

a.text: Remember the promise we made at the beginning of the lesson? Good. Keep your voice low when answering, and don't tell anyone about the classes.
Ray Tanka has been teaching you about our history for the past few months. As for myself, I've been struggling to decide what to teach you in our last lesson.
Mathematics? Language? Agriculture? Weapon-making?
What I've come to realize is that whatever I teach you won't truly change our lives. We've lived silently in despair for too long.
The war eighteen years ago never ended. The ghosts of Leithanien's fleet continue to haunt those who experienced that war.
Many died in despair, drowned in the fear of war and of being consumed by the black rocks that grew from their bodies.
But our instincts drove us to seek a way to overcome despair.
Some declared war on despair, on the outsiders who oppressed us, but they all fell short in the face of cruel reality—

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: ...Came to see the contracts.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: I've never seen a more motivated mercenary than you. Are you trying to buy a mansion in Columbia or something?

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: One should feel lucky just to be alive for so long. In that sense, I suppose your name is well-deserved.

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: I heard a bunch of jobs came in lately. Anything good?

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: There are eyes on and in the city now. Things didn't turn out too well for the last few who took these jobs.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: It's Babel stuff. Are you sure you want to be part of that mess?

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: Yeah. I trust my luck.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Have it your way. There's a teacher in town who's been saying good things about Babel's outsiders. Someone is willing to pay to shut him up for good.

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: ...Will do.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: I look forward to your surprises.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Hope your luck doesn't run out today.
The nomadic city of Kazdel, Kazdel
It has been a while since Goodluck came back.
The city has changed a lot. People come and go. He is familiar with the words 'Babel' and 'Military Commission'; there are always people fighting over things that he does not understand.
He does not understand why the Sarkaz feel the need to fight one another.
He takes out the photo of the target, a mild-mannered young man. The triangular marking on his sleeve seems familiar.
A teacher spreading praise about Babel's outsiders, inciting opposition against the Military Commission.
'Sorry, your luck just ran out today.'

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: Should be around here.

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: Wait... this place...
He's been away for a long time, but not long enough to forget his home.
Odda's home.

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: Odda, you should not have gotten involved...

a.text: We've gotten used to despair from one defeat after another at the hands of powers beyond our ability to resist.
But we needed to convince ourselves that our despair was not self-inflicted, that it stemmed from an obvious source in our lives.
That is what Babel has become for people in this day and age.
It was Babel who brought the enemies. It was Babel's medicine that worsened our Oripathy. It was Babel's education that sapped our will to resist...
It was Babel who deluded the King of Sarkaz and tricked us into giving up on collecting the blood debt from the outsiders. Babel is the source of all our despair.
I see some of you nodding. No doubt you've heard the same from your parents. In desperate times, people often mistake hearsay for the truth.
But is it the truth, though? Were our lives better without outsiders in Kazdel?
Don't take anything at face value. See, think, and find your own answer.
Yes, it's hard to leave Kazdel. The land outside is full of danger. Even making it to the border of the next country is no small feat.
But I'll still leave this place. I'll go to Leithanien, Columbia, Kazimierz, to anywhere that I may find a way to change things.
Then, I'll come back and teach you, and all the children of the Sarkaz.
What will happen to Babel, you ask? The future of Babel—

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: Hide yourselves. Don't make a sound.

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: Hello? Are you looking for someone?

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Sorry, I got the wrong door.

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: Do you need help? I'm familiar with the area.
He smiles. There is no panic in his eyes.
Ascalon scans the sparsely furnished room, and understands.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Do you live here on your own?

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: Yes...

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: My name is Ascalon. I'm from Babel.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Thank you for sheltering him, but you must leave.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Be careful. These are troubled times.

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: You heard her. Someone knows you're here. You need to go.

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: Not just the Military Commission, but also those mercenaries who've been bringing trouble to our doorstep...

steps.name: 'Teacher'
steps.text: I know. I'm very grateful to you for lending us your house to serve as classroom.

steps.name: 'Teacher'
steps.text: The children—

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: I'll take them home. Don't worry, you can continue your classes in a few days, once the storm has passed.

steps.name: 'Teacher'
steps.text: There will be no need. As I've said before, I'm ready to leave.

steps.name: 'Teacher'
steps.text: I've already spent too much time here because I wanted to see the lessons through to the end. There are many places that I still need to see.

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: ...Alright. Oh! Don't forget the potatoes.

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: They're from the children and me. It's not much, but they will serve as a few meals on the road.

steps.name: 'Teacher'
steps.text: Thank you so much... all of you.

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: I should be the one thanking you. I learned a lot from you.

steps.name: 'Teacher'
steps.text: For the past few years, Kazdel has grown faster than its education and public thinking can keep up.

steps.name: 'Teacher'
steps.text: I fear that our powers will be our own destruction, if we do not change the present situation.

steps.name: 'Teacher'
steps.text: The conflicts we see in Kazdel now are a good example. This is not how the Sarkaz should be.

steps.name: 'Teacher'
steps.text: I have yet to find a way to change all these, but I know that the answer does not lie within Kazdel.

steps.name: 'Teacher'
steps.text: Goodbye, Odda.

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: Goodbye... may your journey be safe and smooth.
Odda watches as the 'Teacher' disappears around the corner, but does not go in.
He does not remember when it started, but he has the habit of sitting by the door, waiting for a familiar someone to return.
Wind stirs the dust from the streets, and the dust stirs up his tears. There is not even a shadow.
He gently closes the door.

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: Odda...
Goodluck sees the target leave the house. Then, he sees a familiar figure that he has not seen for a long time.
His blade feels heavy. He cannot move.

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: Odda... I'm sorry... I didn't know...

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: I'm a lousy dad, but...
He tightens his grip on the knife's hilt.
He knows only one way to give Odda a better future.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: ...Another one.
A mist shrouds a corpse in the corner of the street, erasing all traces of its existence.
The passing of a life in Kazdel is akin to a speck of dust falling to the ground, unheard, unceremonious, and unnoticed.
His luck has run out.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: How long do you plan on hiding there, Manfred? Or are you planning to stab me in the back now?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Another mercenary. How many have you killed?

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Didn't see the point to keep count.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: You could kill one, two, a hundred even, but can you kill every single mercenary who accepts the contract?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: They just want to remind us that we've been complacent with the status quo for far too long.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Using the lives of Babel members as a reminder? To remind whom?

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: He made a promise to Her Highness. Is this what he calls 'protection' for Babel? All I see are crackdowns on Babel and mercenaries running wild!

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: There are some things that should not be said aloud. Especially not by you, Ascalon.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: If you don't like it, arrest me.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Let's see if you've improved at all under his tutelage.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: The General has taught me that there are more important things than violence.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: And by the looks of things, the mercenaries aren't the only ruthless cutthroats around here.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Stop dodging if you dare! I'll prove to Their Highnesses that I can beat you!

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Too slow, Manfred.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Wai—

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Argh!

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: You're dead. Again.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Get up.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Don't... need you... to tell... me...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Footwork, Manfred. And Ascalon... stop going for his head all the time?

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: This is the most effective way. It's his own fault for getting hit.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: If he can't dodge it, he has to learn to take it.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: You're right, Ascalon. But why did you stop? We didn't tell you to.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: I... I can take it, Your Highness. It's not over yet!

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Huh? I hit... Your Highness! I hit—

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Did you, now?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Let me down, Ascalon!

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Don't hurt him, Ascalon.
Manfred's long limbs flail helplessly in the air, while his torso is tied to a wooden stake.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: H-How did you do it so fast?!

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Got my inspiration from the way Her Highness sews.
Manfred wriggles to break free, but the more he squirms, the tighter the ropes hug him.
He cannot understand how Ascalon can be so strong and fast, when she looks as thin and frail as him.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Let—me—down!

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Look, I won again!
Ascalon raises her weapon high and grins victoriously at the twin sovereigns.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Ascalon has gotten a lot more cheerful.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: What are you thinking?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: They're different from the other Sarkaz children.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: We can change them, but how can we reach all the children of Kazdel?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Give me time. Babel can do it.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Time is a luxury.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I know. But education is not something that can be rushed. What we're doing is leaving hope for the next generation.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The flame of hope will never go out, as long as a single teacher in Kazdel remains willing to share with these children the vision of a beautiful future.
Theresa casts her eyes towards the two children, full of hope for the future.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Well? Are you going to admit defeat or not?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: No! L-Let me down! We're not done!

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: I'll let you down when you admit defeat.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: No way!

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I'll unbind you, Manfred.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Thank you, Your Highness... W-woah, why am I flying?! Y-Your Highness!

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Hehe.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: ...Hehe.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Alright, that will do, Theresa. Let him down.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: You've improved. But Theresis hasn't taught you everything he knows.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: You were always the faster learner, but ever since you left the general, you've been nothing but unadjusted and lost. He is disappointed in your departure, by the way.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: I may not be as good with words as you are, but at least I don't just ignore the insults against Her Highness Theresa.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Do you really know why Her Highness is so dedicated to Babel's ideals? Do you really know why the General hasn't openly denounced the attacks on Babel?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: You should have talked to him, rather than turning your back on him.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: I turned my back? You're the ones who turned your backs on Her Highness and the voices of so many.

spans.text: back? You're the ones who turned your backs on Her Highness and the voices of so many.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: It's Theresis who has turned a blind eye to the mercenaries' acts of violence and the damage they've caused Babel! This much I know.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: The General has allowed it precisely because he can't ignore the voices of the majority.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: If the fate of the Sarkaz is doomed to fall into the abyss, what's wrong with using more effective means to prevent it?

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: So that's what you truly think.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: It's what most of us in Kazdel think.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: It's not that I don't trust Her Highness... anyone can promise a better future. But we can't ignore the reality before it.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Isn't it crueler to use violence to force a child to shake hands and make peace with the murderer who just killed his father?

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Say whatever you want.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: I'll keep my hands off the Military Commission. But if you try to act through the mercenaries...

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Then my job is simple.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: No more mercenaries, no more problems.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Ascalon!

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: ...If you have the time.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Go visit Her Highness. I've never seen her so tired.
A puff of mist is the only sign that she was ever there.
Manfred looks down and wipes away the blood slowly seeping out of his chest.
He sighs and turns into the empty street, only to spot the deceased mercenary's effects.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Someday... we will all understand.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: It was never Her Highness or the General who made the choice.

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: Who's there?
He hesitates before the door.
It has been a busy day at this old, ramshackle house, from the 'Teacher' to the multiple visitors.
Who could it be outside the door?
Has father finally returned? And if so, what should he say?
He has learned so much from the 'Teacher' that he wants to share with his father, whose visits back home have become less and less frequent.
He takes a deep breath, collects his mind, puts on a calm face, and opens the door.

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: Hello...?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Good evening.

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: You're... er, can I help you, sir?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: You know who I am?

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: No sir, but I know the uniform of the Military Commission.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Just a routine inspection. Do you recognize these items?

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: This is... my father's—!

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: There have been some disturbances in the city, and I'm afraid your father... I'm so sorry.

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: Wh-Where did you find them? Was there...?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: There was nothing else left at the scene. I'm sorry.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: What's your name?

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: ...Odda.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: If you need any help...

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: No... no, I'm very grateful that you brought these back.

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: It's been a long time since I last saw him... this is enough.

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: I don't have to wait anymore... He's not coming back...

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Do you have family? Or friends you can count on?

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: I can take care of myself. Besides, we see things like this every day in this city, no?

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: I-I'm sorry I gushed, sir. I just feel like I know you, somehow...

steps.name: Odda
steps.text: I'm sure you're busy. I won't keep you any longer.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: My condolences.
The door closes. Manfred can hear the sound of sobbing coming from behind the door, but he doesn't feel sorrow. Not anymore.
Odda's right; he's seen this too many times. Yet he remembers this is not what the city was meant to be.
